hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -3}h(x)$ represents the limit of $h$ as $x$ approaches $-3$.

We see that $h(-3)\approx -4$, but the $y$-values seem to approach a different value as the $x$-values approach $-3$.

![The graph of function h has arrows pointing along the curve, rising up to the right and down to the left, respectively, pointing to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/01a2683aefeee8af2d1ef82a5ede488215473b9e)

The limit seems to be somewhere between $y=-6$ and $y=-5$, but slightly closer to $y=-5$.

![The graph of function h has a dashed horizontal line passing through the open circle, between y = negative 5 and y = negative 6, closer to y = negative 5.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e5fa308d990e74fa12214a3722f7f524249ad518)

question.content:
The function $h$ is defined for all real numbers.

![Function h is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve and a closed circle. The curve starts in quadrant 3, moves downward to (negative 5, negative 6), and moves upward through an open circle at x = negative 3, just below y = negative 5. The curve ends in quadrant 4. The closed circle is plotted at x = negative 3, just below y = negative 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/654f9db57ad85501de0707841378e37be91f711c)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -3}h(x)$ ?**
